summary: Trovafloxacin was pulled from the market in the United States and two other countries starting in 1999 because of liver harm [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, it received a high score of 86 for liver risk and a low score of 20 for heart risk [M]. A similar drug named Alatrofloxacin was also pulled from the market in the United States and the European Union for liver harm [4]. Another similar drug, Temafloxacin, was withdrawn worldwide for metabolic and blood-related harm, while Ciprofloxacin carries a boxed warning in the United States for nerve and muscle or bone harm [5][6].
